title: Switching: VLANs, Spanning Tree and MTU

header.html: 2.2 Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features: VLAN, VLAN database, switch virtual interface (SVI); interface configuration (native VLAN, voice VLAN, 802.1Q tagging, link aggregation, speed, duplex); spanning tree; maximum transmission unit (MTU) and jumbo frames
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1VLANs

A virtual LAN (VLAN) splits one physical switch into several logical networks (broadcast domains). Devices in different VLANs need a router or a layer 3 switch to talk.

Term Meaning
VLAN database The switch's list of VLAN IDs and names (IDs 1 to 4094)
Access port Carries one VLAN, untagged, to an end device
Trunk port Carries several VLANs between switches, using 802.1Q tags
802.1Q tagging Adds a 4-byte tag with the VLAN ID to frames on a trunk
Native VLAN The VLAN whose frames cross a trunk untagged; must match on both ends
Voice VLAN A separate VLAN for IP phones so voice gets its own segment and QoS
SVI (switch virtual interface) A layer 3 interface for a VLAN on a layer 3 switch; acts as the VLAN's default gateway

Exam tip

. A native VLAN mismatch causes errors and leaks. Inter-VLAN routing needs an SVI or a router subinterface.

2Interface settings

Setting Notes
Speed 10/100/1000 Mbps or more; both ends should agree (auto-negotiation)
Duplex Full duplex (send and receive together) or half; a mismatch causes collisions, slow speed and errors
Link aggregation Bundles several physical links into one logical link for more bandwidth and redundancy, using LACP (IEEE 802.3ad)

3Spanning tree

Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) prevents layer 2 loops in networks with redundant links by blocking some paths.

Concept Meaning
Root bridge The reference switch chosen by the lowest bridge ID (priority, then MAC address)
Root port Each non-root switch's best path to the root
Designated port Forwarding port for a segment
Blocking/alternate port Blocked to break the loop
States (classic) Blocking, listening, learning, forwarding
RSTP (rapid STP, 802.1w) Converges in seconds instead of tens of seconds

Exam tip

. The root bridge is the switch with the lowest priority; ties go to the lowest MAC address. Without STP a broadcast storm can bring down the network.

4MTU and jumbo frames

The maximum transmission unit (MTU) is the largest frame payload an interface sends: 1500 bytes for standard Ethernet. Jumbo frames (about 9000 bytes) cut overhead for storage and data center traffic but every device on the path must support them.

Exam tip

. Trunk ports carry tagged VLANs; access ports carry one untagged VLAN. A native VLAN mismatch causes problems.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Two switches must carry traffic for several VLANs over one link. What should be configured?

  • AAn access port in VLAN 1
  • BA port mirror
  • CAn 802.1Q trunk
  • DA spanning tree blocking port
Show the answer

Answer: C. Trunks carry multiple tagged VLANs.

S2VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 hosts cannot communicate. What is needed?

  • AA larger MTU
  • BA router or layer 3 switch with SVIs
  • CA second spanning tree instance
  • DLink aggregation between the hosts
Show the answer

Answer: B. Different VLANs need layer 3 routing.

S3A redundant triangle of switches suffers a broadcast storm. Which protocol should prevent this?

  • ASpanning Tree Protocol
  • BLink Aggregation Control Protocol
  • C802.1Q tagging
  • DSimple Network Management Protocol
Show the answer

Answer: A. STP blocks redundant paths to prevent loops.

S4Which switch becomes the spanning tree root bridge by default?

  • AThe switch with the most ports
  • BThe switch with the lowest bridge priority, then lowest MAC address
  • CThe switch with the highest MAC address
  • DThe newest switch
Show the answer

Answer: B. The lowest bridge ID wins.

S5Four 1 Gbps links must act as one logical link for bandwidth and redundancy. Which feature fits?

  • ASpanning tree
  • BLink aggregation with LACP
  • CPort security
  • DVoice VLAN
Show the answer

Answer: B. LACP bundles links into one logical link.

S6Which setting keeps IP phone traffic on its own segment?

  • AThe native VLAN
  • BJumbo frames
  • CA switch virtual interface only
  • DA voice VLAN
Show the answer

Answer: D. A voice VLAN separates phone traffic.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does 802.1Q do?

Show the answer

Adds a VLAN tag to frames on a trunk.

R2What is the standard Ethernet MTU?

Show the answer

1500 bytes.

R3What does an SVI provide?

Show the answer

A layer 3 interface for a VLAN (its default gateway).

R4What protocol aggregates links?

Show the answer

LACP.

R5What does RSTP improve?

Show the answer

Convergence speed.

R6What happens to native VLAN traffic on a trunk?

Show the answer

It crosses untagged.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
VLAN IDs 1-4094; access vs trunk; 802.1Q; native VLAN untagged; voice VLAN; SVI
Interface speed and duplex must match; LACP link aggregation
STP root bridge (lowest ID), root, designated, blocked; RSTP faster
MTU 1500 standard; jumbo about 9000, support end to end
